title: Choose the visual world for $PADS
question: The roll assigned Lily Pad Central, a split-flap departures board where every sitter is a row that never departs. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Lily Pad Central
options.lineage: Solari split-flap departure boards in old railway halls
options.thesis: The site is a station departures board, and Sitwell is the one passenger who never boards.
options.viewport: A full-width departures board: NEXT FEEDING 20:00 WIB, the fly jar total and the top sitters flip into place; Sitwell sits on the bench beneath; BOARD ON PONS and the CA ticket sit on the board's own footer rail.
options.risk: If the flaps are drawn timidly it reads as a skin; the flip motion and strict board grid must carry it.

raised.raise: Every wallet row is its own addressable URL, shareable as a ticket.
Irreversibility gets its own material: a hopped-off flap locks red and never flips again.
One monumental number per section, with quiet station wall between dense boards.
Every figure carries its source label (block, tx) pinned beside it.
Full traceability: feeding total → each recipient row → its tx.

options.label: The Sitting Hall
options.lineage: zazen meditation halls and their bell schedules
options.thesis: Holding is sitting meditation; feeding time is the evening bell.
options.viewport: Sitwell on his pad inside an ink enso, an unbroken-sit counter and the next bell time beneath.
options.risk: Calm can undersell to a degen audience; the most familiar 'diamond hands = zen' framing.

options.label: Weekly Manga Page
options.lineage: weekly shonen manga, screentone and speed lines
options.thesis: $PADS as a weekly manga: every feeding is a new chapter page.
options.viewport: A right-to-left page where Sitwell refuses to jump in the decisive black panel; the CA sits in a speech bubble.
options.case: Fuses well and CT loves the register (audience identification holds); loses on clarity because live numbers and a wallet checker fight the panel grid.
options.risk: Numbers-heavy sections read awkward inside panels.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: The pond as a one-bit card stack.
options.viewport: A single card with Sitwell dithered and buttons to flip cards.
options.case: Fuses poorly: traders don't identify with it and one-bit hides live data.
options.kept: Every row addressable as its own URL.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Holding as a print developing; selling pulls it too early.
options.viewport: A print of Sitwell emerging in the tray as pad days count up.
options.case: Strong metaphor for irreversibility, weak audience identification.
options.kept: Irreversible states get their own material.
options.risk: Moody and slow for a memecoin.

options.label: Fashion Flagship
options.viewport: One huge Sitwell look with a single serif word.
options.case: Loses both axes for a degen trader.
options.kept: One monumental figure per section with real quiet around it.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: Holders as tension holding the column up.
options.viewport: A breathing column whose cords are the sitters.
options.kept: Labels pinned to their source values.

options.label: Jacquard Brocade
options.viewport: A loom weaving Sitwell row by row.
options.kept: Traceability from total to every thread.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A memecoin landing page: big mascot hero, ticker, CA copy, stats row, how-it-works steps, leaderboard table.
canonCard.viewport: Mascot left, ticker and buy button right, stat cards under it.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other token on the VPS by design.
